implementation: Modern multi-round dispatch starts total-budget accounting before its first wire leg, checks exhaustion after input fulfilment/state pacing and before each retry, and carries the remaining maxTotalTimeout alongside the original per-leg timeout. Retry options retain signal/progress/reset/headers, force the inner manual-result boundary and omit first-leg resumption/related-request options. Round-cap ordering remains unchanged.

paired.scope: Actual pinned Client multi-round driver with deterministic Date.now and pacing-clock collaborator versus Native dispatch with the same first-leg/leg clock advances. Exact/negative/zero/one-ms budgets, first-leg accounting, shrinking multi-round budgets, round-cap precedence and retry option ownership; results, raw typed errors/data, progress and retry options compare exactly.

native.scope: Actual localhost HTTP first input-required response plus real 250ms pacing exhausts a 100ms flow budget without sending a second leg; default cache/output x86/x64 workers, modern dispatch/negotiation, manager/supervision/resources and HTTP/stdio consumers.

cleanup.scope: All owned test workspaces/home/tmp removed after the final consumer; logs/XML, raw HTTP packets, paired observations and hashes retained.

limitations: This closes the multi-round retry budget contract. Per-wire-leg timer reset/progress, arbitrary abort reason wrapping and serving ProtocolError conversion remain separate pending contracts.
The original checks this budget at retry/progress boundaries; this implementation does not introduce a different hard wall-clock timer.
Targeted verification only, without production pin promotion or full release qualification.
